commits.summary: Add symbolic, capability and TLA+ verification examples 006 to 012
commits.body:
The first five examples enumerate a finite state machine, which a type system could approximate. This adds three approaches that a type system cannot, each with examples aimed at cloud Java developers: B9 regression verification, B10 capability contracts and D1 protocol model checking. The examples generator (examples/tools/build.py) now has one runner per approach id, the result schema gained verdictLabel, domain, proof, statement, trace and related fields, and the table of contents shows the approach.

B9, regression verification (examples 006 to 008): Equivalence.java in examples/tools/contracts compares two compiled versions of a method with unbounded inputs. It relocates the old classes into a 'before' package by rewriting constant pools (Relocate.java), generates a harness that asserts both versions agree on every input outside an optional --unchanged-unless Java expression, and runs JBMC on the bytecode with java.lang.Math's real class on the classpath. A counterexample is replayed on the JVM; small inputs are searched first so the witness is readable. HoldPolicy.totalCents gained a 10% group discount for six seats or more to have realistic arithmetic to verify. 006 refutes a per-seat rounding refactor, 007 proves a doubled discount confined to seats >= 6 over all 2^96 inputs in 13 s, 008 shows a declared scope (seats >= 8) that a one-formula rewrite violates. Measured limit, recorded in the README: an unchanged region with a 64-bit division on each side does not finish in 10 min with MiniSat, Z3, cvc5 or --refine.

B10, capability contracts (examples 009 and 010): Capabilities.java derives, from a module's compiled classes, every call to a JDK entry point of a capability (clock, console, environment, filesystem, JNDI, native, network, process, randomness, reflection, scripting, serialization, threads) and the libraries called, as src/contract/capabilities.contract, checked by the same verifyContracts task (the Gradle plugin now passes --classes and --module; -Ptarget=capabilities adds the contract). The contracts and ticketing-domain modules have baseline contracts with no capabilities. 009 catches MessageCodec resolving a class named in a Kafka payload with Class.forName, the shape of the Jackson deserialization CVEs; 010 shows a serialization setting that changes nothing.

D1, protocol model checking (examples 011 and 012): examples/apps/boxoffice/spec/BoxOffice.tla models the two services, their outbox relays, Kafka topics, the sweeper and the clock, one action per transaction, with the README's safety invariants. Its order state machine, OrderLifecycleContract.tla, is generated by examples/tools/tla/contract_to_tla.py from the B8 behavioural contract, so the model runs the decisions the bytecode is proven to make. 011 removes the heldBy query in PaymentEventHandler and TLC produces a nine-step trace in which a paid customer's capture event is dead-lettered after the hold expires; 012 deletes the hold sweeper and TLC confirms every invariant in 3,604 states. The generator runs TLC with one worker so the trace is stable.

Verified by running the verifier's 17 unit tests (jbmc installed) and python3 examples/tools/build.py for all twelve examples, each reaching its expected verdict; the first five pages regenerate unchanged apart from the new table column. Documentation updated: examples/README.md (approach table and intro), approaches.md (B9, B10, D1 and the JBMC finding), the contracts README (three contract kinds, limits), the spec README, the Box Office README, the root README and the setup README. These land in one commit because the generator, schemas and tables are shared by all three approaches.

commits.summary: Credit example authors and commit the TLA+ standard modules
commits.body:
examples/README.md now opens with a note that examples 001 to 005 were created by Opus 5.5 and 006 to 012 by Fable 5.1, and suggests reading the Fable examples first.

The /tmp/Naturals.tla, /tmp/Sequences.tla and /tmp/FiniteSets.tla paths in the verifier output of examples 011 and 012 were never lost work: TLC unpacks its standard modules from tla2tools.jar into a temporary directory and deletes them on exit. Unmodified copies from TLC 2.19 (rev 5a47802), with the MIT licence, now live in examples/tools/tla/standard-modules, and build.py passes that directory as -DTLA-Library so TLC parses them and the evidence names files that exist. The fallback to a tlc wrapper on PATH does not pass the library and still prints temporary paths.

Verified by regenerating examples 011 and 012, which keep their expected verdicts, and by comparing the three modules byte for byte with the jar.

commits.summary: Reword the note on which examples to read first
commits.body: The maintainer reworded the opening note of examples/README.md to say that the Fable examples go significantly beyond what type checking can achieve. All twelve examples were regenerated before this commit and kept their expected verdicts; the regenerated evidence differed only in per-run values and was not kept.

commits.summary: Add hand-written session notes to the trace summaries
commits.body:
One session's trace needed explaining and its generated summary cannot be edited: session 560d5e98 wrote a blog post that was committed to the Terminal-Value repo, and its Changes section lists the 006 to 012 commit, which another session made, because that commit carries the only trailer linking the log with the blog work.

An optional llm-dlc/session-notes/<session-id>.md now appears as a Notes section near the top of that session's summary, and check scans it for secrets. Commits and trailers are left as they are. Summaries of sessions without a note come out byte for byte the same, confirmed by re-syncing them. The first note records the blog work and the misattributed entry.

commits.summary: Link the blog post now that it is on GitHub
commits.body: The note on session 560d5e98 named the Terminal-Value commit that holds the blog post in plain text because that commit was not yet on GitHub. It is now, so the note links to the commit and the post's folder, pinned to that commit so the links keep showing what the session wrote. This commit also carries the trace metadata recorded by the previous push. Both URLs returned 200 before committing.

commits.summary: Generate a traces overview at llm-dlc/traces/README.md
commits.body:
The session index gave one row per session and nothing across them. The new page adds every session up: totals, a table per session, tokens and cache share, tool use, every commit with its sessions and logs, log storage, and the session notes. It closes with how to read the numbers.

sync.py renders it on every sync from llm-dlc/traces-readme-template.md, using only the manifests and session notes, so it needs no logs and comes out the same on each run. check now fails if the file does not match the manifests. Commit totals count a commit shared by two sessions once. There are no dollar figures, because manifests do not record what a call was billed.

Verified by comparing the totals with an independent sum over the manifests (75 prompts, 459 model calls, 643 tool calls, 17 unique commits against 18 listed per session) and by appending a line to the page and seeing check report one error, then pass once it was restored.

commits.summary: Run the trace pipeline on commit and push, not on every turn
commits.body:
The Stop hook rewrote tracked files and stamped @ after every turn, and each push recorded its own commit's SHA afterwards, so the repo could never be clean. A session's tail, and a session with no commits, also had no log a commit pointed at: nothing uploaded them, so their summaries linked to a 404.

Tracked trace files now change only on commit and push. Stop and SessionEnd only feed Langfuse. A PostToolUse hook traces a plain jj commit or git commit by reopening the new commit and syncing into it, so it carries its trailer and manifest however it was made. sync.py push records everything outstanding in one last Record session traces commit, moves the bookmark to it, uploads, checks and pushes, then writes nothing, leaving @ empty. It refuses to run over uncommitted work, and a repeat push makes no commit. A manifest cannot contain its own commit's SHA, so the next commit records it. The /publish skill, run only by the user, wraps commit and push.

Verified end to end in a throwaway clone with a local bare remote and a stubbed CDN upload: the Stop hook left the repo unchanged; plain jj commit, a partial jj commit and git commit were each traced, and re-running the hook changed nothing; push refused uncommitted work, published a tail and a session with no commits, left @ empty, and a second push was a no-op. That test found and fixed a bug: jj abandons an empty @ when another change is edited. No real push or upload was made.

commits.summary: Correct the definition of session status
commits.body: Sessions are now marked ended by the next sync once their transcript has been idle for 10 minutes, because the SessionEnd hook no longer writes the manifest. The specification still described the old rule.
Brings the published traces up to this point: conversation that came after a session's last commit, and sessions with no commit of their own.
